findings.title: Lost wake-up: mc-log waits on a signal that already came
findings.summary: mc_logger[1] signalled condition variable 0x00000051cd514018 at 9669.54 ms when no thread was waiting on it, then joined mc-log. mc-log only began its wait 696.53 ms later and was still blocked 3630.78 ms on, until the end of the trace, with no further signal: the program is hung.
findings.qnx_note: pthread_cond_signal() wakes a thread that is already waiting; with no waiter the signal is lost. Wait in a loop that re-checks the condition while holding the mutex (the thread that sets the condition must also hold the mutex), and test the stop flag before every wait.

findings.title: Unusual behaviour in mc-log
findings.summary: mc-log (prio 10) behaved unlike healthy QNX programs in 180 of its 222 time windows; the most unusual stretch lasted 3600 ms. It stands out in: time waiting on a condition variable (higher than healthy), longest single block (higher than healthy), time asleep (lower than healthy). The closest pattern TraceLens has seen is priority inversion while waiting on a condition variable, but only loosely (distance 9.83 against 0.847 typical for it): treat this as behaviour of its own.
findings.qnx_note: Learned from healthy QNX 8.0 traces: this thread behaved unlike any healthy run in the features listed. It is not a proven bug and gets no automatic fix: look at the timeline around it. Any resemblance to a known pattern is measured against labelled example windows, never a rule that fired.
